indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the other, so it holds it inside

explanation.surface: Someone broods on the poor way they have been treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse is a noun for harsh or improper treatment, a synonym of ill-treatment.

clue.text: US artist captures head of turbot, a fish

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the artist's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Man Ray was an American surrealist photographer and painter

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An American painter depicts a turbot in his picture of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The manta ray is a huge flat ocean fish related to sharks, so it is a fish.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to settle a deal or contest for certain
second meaning: to stitch a tear closed

explanation.surface: A repair job is finished off well.
explanation.definitionFit: To sew up means both to mend with stitches and, idiomatically, to secure an outcome.

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
a seer is a prophet or sage

explanation.surface: A sensible traveller sounds like a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer is someone who visits places of interest, which is what a tourist does.

clue.text: Girl boxing star in US gambling centre

indicators.note: boxing here means putting in a box, enclosing something else

parts.note: Vega is a bright star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A female boxer stars at a fight in Nevada's famous gambling resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas in Nevada is the best-known casino city in the United States.

clue.text: What a relief, getting changed, some time later

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the exclamation are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief on finally getting into fresh clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning eventually, once some time has passed.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Shakespeare's heroine who disguises herself as Cesario
second meaning: a stringed instrument a little larger than a violin

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character owns a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night, and the instrument is a member of the violin family, loosely a fiddle.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1995 James Bond movie
second meaning: a diving sea duck with yellow eyes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Film duck' suggests a cartoon duck; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is both a Pierce Brosnan Bond movie and the name of a diving waterfowl species.

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are lifted straight out of the next words

parts.note: the end of the surname runs into the next word
the opening letter of the theatre name

explanation.surface: A performer named Henderson plays a piece at the Apollo theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition, usually in several movements, for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Gen we translated involving a cultural movement

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the rearranged letters wrap around another piece
translating turns words into another form, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A translator renders a piece of 'gen' about some cultural trend.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age names the alternative spiritual and cultural trend that grew from the 1970s counterculture.

clue.text: Corset found on street — now there's a surprise!

parts.note: a roll-on is an elasticated corset or girdle

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to find a corset lying in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The corset is placed on, that is after, the street abbreviation. 'Stroll on!' is a British exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroll on is an informal British interjection expressing astonishment or incredulity.

clue.text: An hors d'oeuvre, perhaps a favourite, is brought in for each

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so these pieces go within the word for each

parts.note: per means for each, as in ten pounds per head

explanation.surface: A waiter brings a favourite starter in for every diner.
explanation.definitionFit: An hors d'oeuvre is one example of a small dish served before the main meal, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: First of shots with new 'Ping' iron's on one of the greens

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only
new means made afresh, so the letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A golfer with a new Ping-brand iron plays a shot onto one of the greens.
explanation.walkthrough: Ping is a golf club maker and greens sound like putting greens, but the greens are vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Greens are green vegetables, and the spring onion, a young onion eaten raw, is one of them.

parts.note: dept is the shortened form of department

explanation.surface: A specialist works in a downsized department.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept and expert are synonyms, both meaning highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Like a shot, moves swiftly across the City, in a straight line

indicators.note: one piece stretches across another, lying on either side of it

parts.note: a throw is a shot, as at a coconut shy
EC is the postcode of the City of London
to fly is to move swiftly

explanation.surface: Someone races across the City of London like a bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes start EC.
explanation.definitionFit: As the crow flies is an idiom for the direct straight-line distance between two places.

clue.text: First-rate crumble, pie brought over in restaurant

indicators.note: bringing something over turns it upside down, which in a down clue reverses the letter order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
to rot is to crumble away

explanation.surface: Diners order a top-notch crumble and pie in an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumble and pie look like puddings on a menu; here crumble is a verb meaning decay.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating place, a kind of restaurant.

indicators.note: repackaged means put up in a new form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A drug company relaunches a vital remedy to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative and profitable are synonyms, both meaning producing plenty of money.

clue.text: Battle scene force before heavy blows

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics
a lander is a heavy punch that lands

explanation.surface: A battlefield where an army attacks before artillery strikes hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Flanders, in Belgium, saw some of the bloodiest fighting of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders was the scene of major First World War battles such as Ypres and Passchendaele.

clue.text: English actor in western with odd name, thriller about cattle, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround another piece
odd means strange or irregular, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English actor stars in a cowboy film that is an odd cattle-rustling thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Warren Mitchell is best known as the bigot Alf Garnett in the BBC sitcom Till Death Us Do Part.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren Mitchell was a London-born stage and television performer, so he is an English actor.

explanation.surface: Dinner is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'nearly' but supplies the short Latin-derived word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Repast is a formal or literary word for a meal.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a run conceded in cricket that is not scored off the bat
second meaning: surplus, more than is needed

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire signals a wide delivered during an over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach; it adds a run to the score that is not credited to the batter. An over is a set of six balls, which tempts you to read it as cricket too.
explanation.definitionFit: Wides, no-balls and byes are all cricket extras, and as an adjective the word also means surplus or left over.

indicators.note: beheaded means the head is cut off, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman who started a fire is executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-raising is the British legal term for the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an enterprise or campaign carried out
second meaning: a surgical procedure on a patient

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests an undertaker in an operating theatre; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a planned enterprise, such as a military campaign, and a single surgical procedure.

indicators.note: the possessive marks the letters as belonging to, held within, the name before it

parts.note: spans the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A work by the American sculptor Temima Gezari.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a carved or sculpted representation of a person or god, so a sculpture.

clue.text: A bad-tempered moment reportedly caused by a puzzle

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: cross means bad-tempered and a tick is a moment

explanation.surface: A solver has a brief fit of temper brought on by a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which the initial letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: Plagiarist could make head of publishing very angry

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A copycat writer might infuriate the boss of a publishing house.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate in the literary sense is someone who reproduces another's work without permission.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: instruction in a skill
second meaning: exercising in a gym

explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' looks like solving a problem, but here it is physical exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both teaching someone a skill and the physical exercise an athlete does.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a break, as when Parliament or a school stops sitting
second meaning: an alcove or niche in a wall

explanation.surface: Someone spends their break by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both a period when a legislature or school is on break and a hollow set back in a wall.
